# Running the notebooks {#sec-running}

## Three ways to use this companion

1. **Read the website.** The live panels run in the browser with no installation.
2. **Run the code in Google Colab.** Every chapter starts with an **Open in Colab** button. Colab is free and runs in the browser;
   you only need a Google account. Use *File → Save a copy in Drive* to keep your changes.
3. **Run it on your computer** with Jupyter, or rebuild the whole book with Quarto.

## Installation

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt     # numpy scipy matplotlib pandas jupyter ipywidgets
quarto preview                      # live preview while editing
quarto render                       # builds _book/ (HTML)
```

Rendering executes every Python cell once. Results are cached in `_freeze/` (`freeze: auto`), so later builds only re-run the
chapters you changed.

## Publishing the website (GitHub Pages)

The source lives at <https://github.com/{{< var github_user >}}/{{< var repo >}}> (folder `{{< var subdir >}}/`) and the site at
<https://{{< var github_user >}}.github.io/{{< var repo >}}/{{< var subdir >}}/>. After editing a chapter:

```bash
cd notebooks && python build_notebooks.py && cd ..         # refresh the notebooks (Colab buttons point to them)
git add -A && git commit -m "Update chapter 4" && git push   # update the source on GitHub
bash ../publish.sh                                         # render and update the website
```

## Regenerating the notebooks

```bash
cd notebooks
python build_notebooks.py
```

The script converts every chapter, adds a setup cell that works both locally and in Colab (it downloads `laserlib.py` from
GitHub when running in Colab), and rebuilds `interactive_explorers.ipynb`.

## The `laserlib` module

| function | purpose |
|---|---|
| `kT`, `photon_energy_eV`, `wavelength_from_eV`, `dB`, `CM3`, `CM2` | units and conversions (SI inside, eV for energies) |
| `mode_density`, `count_modes_box`, `planck_rho`, `rayleigh_jeans_rho`, `planck_emittance` | radiation in a box |
| `A_over_B`, `stim_over_spont` | Einstein coefficients |
| `three_level`, `four_level`, `pump_power_3level` | level systems and pumping |
| `lorentzian`, `gaussian`, `voigt`, `doppler_fwhm`, `lifetime_fwhm` | line shapes |
| `er_cross_sections`, `edfa_gain_uniform`, `edfa_propagate`, `edfa_nsp`, `edfa_nf` | erbium-doped fiber amplifier |
| `mode_number`, `mode_spacing`, `threshold_gain`, `photon_lifetime`, `threshold_inversion`, `gas_laser_output`, `finesse`, `fp_transmission` | Fabry–Perot laser cavity |
| `qswitch_energy_fraction`, `qswitch_pulse`, `mode_locked_field` | pulsed lasers |
| `fermi_half`, `quasi_fermi`, `gain_spectrum_bulk`, `delta_F`, `peak_gain_slide`, `n_for_gain_slide` | semiconductor gain |
| `facet_R`, `ld_threshold`, `ld_power`, `ld_efficiencies`, `extraction_efficiency` | laser diode static characteristics |
| `ld_rate_equations`, `ld_step_response`, `ld_small_signal`, `relaxation_frequency`, `turn_on_delay` | laser diode dynamics |
| `qw_infinite`, `qw_finite` | quantum wells |
| `bragg_wavelength`, `dfb_modes`, `grating_rt`, `dbr_reflectance` | gratings, DFB lasers, DBR mirrors |
| `fp_amplifier_gain`, `saturated_gain` | optical amplifiers |
| `hermite_gauss`, `resonator_g`, `transverse_mode_freqs`, `waist_from_resonator` | beams and resonators |
| `schawlow_townes` | laser linewidth |

`laser_sim.js` contains JavaScript ports of `er_cross_sections`, `edfa_propagate`, `grating_rt`, `dbr_reflectance`, the rate
equations, the free-carrier gain and an FFT, used by the live panels. Every function was checked against the worked examples of
the slides (see the "worked example" sections).
